posts.why: Every business has an FAQ they have never written down.

tiktok.hook: This site answers six questions nowhere. Price, delivery, hours, location, returns, payment.
tiktok.vo: This site answers six questions nowhere. Price. Delivery. Opening hours. Where they are. Returns. How to pay. Every customer asks at least four of those before buying, which means every customer costs you a conversation you did not need to have. Put the six answers on the page and the conversations become orders.
tiktok.cap: Six questions. Every customer asks them. Nowhere on the page.

instagram.cap: All six are already typed in your inbox. Screenshot them and put them on the site.

facebook.body:
Count the questions your customers ask before they buy. For most businesses it is four to six:

Price. Delivery. Opening hours. Location. Returns. How to pay.

Most of those are answered nowhere on the website, which means every single customer costs you a conversation you did not need to have.

The answers are already sitting in your inbox. Search one word and you will find them typed out fifty times.

Which one do you answer most?

posts.why: Turns an annoyance into an obvious, cheap fix.

tiktok.hook: You have typed the same answer four hundred times this year.
beats: That is not service, that is a missing page
tiktok.vo: You have typed the same answer four hundred times this year. Same words, different customers, all day. That is not good service. That is a missing page on your website, and it is costing you the hours you would have spent actually making the thing you sell.
tiktok.cap: If you have typed it more than twenty times, it belongs on the page.

instagram.cap: Your thumbs are doing work your website should do.

facebook.body:
If you have typed the same answer more than twenty times this year, it does not belong in the chat. It belongs on the page.

Same words, different customers, all day. That is not good service. That is a missing page, and it is costing you the hours you would have spent making the thing you actually sell.

What is the sentence you type most often?

Put it on your website tonight and count the difference by Friday.

posts.why: A free fix, doable in one minute, on the platform they already use.

tiktok.hook: Put four answers in your WhatsApp away message. Free night shift.
tiktok.vo: Put your four answers in your WhatsApp away message. One line for the price, one for delivery, one for hours, one for how to pay. Then when someone messages at eleven at night, they get an answer instead of silence, and you wake up to a conversation that has already started properly. That is a night shift for free.
tiktok.cap: Four lines in an away message. It answers when you are asleep.

instagram.cap: You cannot hire a night shift for ₦0. Except here.

facebook.body:
Put your four most common answers in your WhatsApp away message.

One line for price. One for delivery. One for opening hours. One for how to pay.

Then when someone messages at 11pm, they get information instead of silence, and you wake up to a conversation that has already started properly.

Four lines. About ninety seconds of typing. It answers while you sleep.

What would your four lines say?

posts.why: Reverses the standard objection in one line.

tiktok.hook: An FAQ page is not lazy. Your inbox is lazy.
tiktok.vo: An FAQ page is not lazy. Your inbox is lazy. If you answer the same question in a chat, one person learns it once. If you answer it on a page, everyone learns it forever, including the people who would never have messaged you, which is most of them.
tiktok.cap: Answering in a chat helps one person. Answering online helps everyone.

instagram.cap: The people who never messaged are the ones an FAQ wins.

facebook.body:
An FAQ page is not lazy. Answering the same question in ten separate chats is the lazy option, because it only helps ten people.

Answer it once, on a page, and it helps everyone who reads it forever — including the people who would never have messaged you. Which is most of them.

What question are you answering over and over that should be written down?

posts.why: A number that makes the wasted effort physically obvious.

tiktok.hook: A vendor typed the word "delivery" three hundred times in one month.
beats: Would have saved all of it
tiktok.vo: A vendor typed the word delivery three hundred times in one month. Same answer every time: yes we deliver, it is this much, it takes this long. Two lines in the catalogue would have saved every one of those replies. That is not a marketing problem, it is a filing problem, and it is free to fix.
tiktok.cap: Three hundred replies to one question. Two lines would have done it.

instagram.cap: Count your most-repeated sentence this month. That number is your wasted hours.

facebook.body:
A vendor typed the word 'delivery' three hundred times in one month.

Every time, the same answer: yes we deliver, it costs this much, it takes this long.

Two lines in their catalogue would have saved all three hundred replies.

That is not a marketing problem. It is a filing problem, and it is free to fix this evening.

What is your most-repeated sentence?

posts.topic: The saved reply you should write tonight
posts.why: One action, tonight, that they will actually do.

tiktok.hook: Tonight, write one saved reply: the answer you typed most this week.
tiktok.vo: Tonight, write one saved reply. Go into your chat, scroll up, find the answer you typed most this week, copy it exactly as you wrote it, and save it as a shortcut on your phone. Not a template from a book, your own words. Tomorrow it takes two taps instead of twenty.
tiktok.cap: Your own words, saved once, used forever. Tonight, two minutes.

instagram.cap: Do not use a template. Use the sentence you already know works.

facebook.body:
Tonight's task, and it takes two minutes.

Open your chat. Scroll up. Find the answer you typed most this week. Copy it exactly as you wrote it — your own words, not a template from a book — and save it as a shortcut on your phone.

Tomorrow that reply takes two taps instead of twenty seconds of thought.

What is yours? Write it in the comments and I will tell you if it is clear.

posts.topic: "Is it available?" is the whole conversation
posts.why: A blunt, memorable reframe of what a product page is for.

tiktok.hook: "Is it available?" is the entire conversation, and it should not exist.
tiktok.vo: Is it available is the entire conversation, and it should not exist. Nobody asks whether a price is nice or a fabric is soft first. They ask whether it is there. So show what is there: a photo, a count, a colour, a size. Stock is more persuasive than any adjective you can write.
tiktok.cap: Show stock, not adjectives.

slides: So answer it before they ask
instagram.cap: A photo of the actual item in the actual size does more than a paragraph.

facebook.body:
The first question almost every customer asks is not about price or quality. It is 'is it available?'

So show what is there. A photo, a count, a colour, a size, a date it can be collected.

Stock is more persuasive than any adjective you can write about the product.

Do your customers have to ask?

posts.topic: What do you ask before buying from a new shop?
posts.why: The answer surprises almost everyone selling online.

tiktok.hook: I asked what people check before buying from a new shop.
tiktok.vo: I asked what people ask before buying from a shop they have never used. It was not the price. It was not the quality. It was where are you, and then, is this a real business. Trust comes before money in every single answer, which is why the location line and the photo of your actual shop matter more than your logo.
tiktok.cap: "Where are you?" came first. Not price. Trust, then money.

instagram.cap: Nobody buys from a stranger without checking they exist.

facebook.body:
I asked people what they check before buying from a shop they have never used.

The order was consistent:
1. Where are you?
2. Is this a real business?
3. Has anyone else bought?
4. How much?

Price came fourth. Trust comes before money every time, which is why an address, a photo of the actual shop, and one real customer sentence matter more than any logo.

What do you check first?

posts.why: Sells a specific deliverable, not a vague improvement.

tiktok.hook: The chat pack includes a four-answer profile setup. It takes one afternoon.
tiktok.vo: The chat pack includes a four answer profile setup, and it is the least exciting page in the whole thing. Price, delivery, hours, payment. Four lines on your profile and in your away message. It takes one afternoon and it answers most of the questions you answer by hand. Five thousand naira for the pack. It will not bring you customers. It stops you losing hours.
tiktok.cap: Four lines, one afternoon, most of your repeated replies gone. ₦5,000. Message PLAYBOOK on WhatsApp: 0905 069 0837.

instagram.cap: The least exciting page is the one that keeps the most hours.

facebook.body:
The least exciting part of the Chat-to-Customer Playbook is the four-answer profile setup.

Price. Delivery. Opening hours. How to pay.

Four lines in your bio and your away message. One afternoon of work. It removes most of the questions you currently answer by hand, one customer at a time.

₦5,000 for the pack. Message PLAYBOOK on WhatsApp: 0905 069 0837. No consulting, no guarantees, no new customers — just fewer wasted hours.

posts.why: A principle with an obvious cost attached.

tiktok.hook: Someone asked us to hide delivery cost until checkout. We said no.
beats: Surprise fees cost more than the fee
tiktok.vo: Someone asked us to keep the delivery cost out of sight until checkout. We said no. It is legal and it works, briefly, and then it costs more than the fee itself, because the customer feels caught rather than served. Show delivery early, even when it is ugly. The ones who stay are the ones who can pay, which is the only kind you want.
tiktok.cap: A surprise fee costs more than the fee. Every time.

slides: The surprise costs more than the fee
instagram.cap: Filters out the buyers who cannot pay, which is a kindness to both sides.

facebook.body:
Someone asked us to keep the delivery cost out of sight until checkout.

We said no. It is legal, and it works briefly, and then it costs more than the fee itself — because the customer feels caught rather than served. They abandon, and they tell people why.

Show delivery early, even when it is ugly. The ones who stay are the ones who can actually pay, which is the only kind of customer worth chasing.

Would you rather lose them early or late?

posts.why: Removes the excuse of not being ready.

tiktok.hook: One item beats a catalogue you have not built yet.
beats: Start with the one that sells most
tiktok.vo: One catalogue item beats a catalogue you have not built. Start with the one that sells most, not your favourite one. A photo, a price, a size, and one sentence about who it is for. Put it on a page. Then add the second item next week. Ten pages built one at a time is a website. A plan for ten pages is still a plan.
tiktok.cap: Start with the item that sells most. Not your favourite.

instagram.cap: Ten pages built one at a time is a website. A plan is still a plan.

facebook.body:
One catalogue item beats a catalogue you have not built yet.

Start with the one that sells most, not your favourite. A photo, a price, a size, and one sentence about who it is for. Put it on a page.

Add the second item next week.

Ten pages built one at a time is a website. Ten pages you are planning is still a plan.

What is your single best seller?

posts.topic: A quote that is one line
posts.why: Recognisable to anyone who has ever sent a quote.

tiktok.hook: This quote is one line: ₦180,000, let me know.
tiktok.vo: This quote is one line. One hundred and eighty thousand naira, let me know. No scope, so they do not know what they are buying. No date, so they cannot plan. No reason, so it is a number with no story. The price was not the problem. The other three lines were missing.
tiktok.cap: Three words were missing, and none of them was the price.

instagram.cap: A number without a story is just a hurdle.

facebook.body:
A quote I saw this week was one line: '₦180,000, let me know.'

No scope, so the customer does not know what they are buying. No date, so they cannot plan. No reason, so the number has nothing holding it up.

The price was not the problem. Three lines were missing around it.

What does your quote usually look like?

posts.topic: A quote with no date is a question
posts.why: The sharpest reframe in the day.

tiktok.hook: A quote with no date is a question, not a quote.
tiktok.vo: A quote with no date is not a quote, it is a question, because the customer cannot answer it. They do not know whether yes means next week or December, so they ask more questions, and every question is another chance for the sale to die. Give them a date and they can say yes.
tiktok.cap: A date turns a number into a decision.

instagram.cap: Every unanswerable sentence in a quote is a delay you cannot afford.

facebook.body:
A quote with no date is not a quote. It is a question.

The customer cannot answer it, because they do not know whether yes means next week or December. So they ask more questions, and every question is another chance for the sale to quietly die.

Give them a date and the sentence becomes answerable.

When will you deliver? Write it in your next quote.

posts.why: The most saveable post of the week.

tiktok.hook: Five lines every quote needs. Copy these labels.
tiktok.vo: Five lines every quote needs. What it is. How much. By when. What is included. And what is not included. That is the entire format, in that order, on one screen, in the message itself. The last line is the one that wins work, and it is the one almost nobody writes.
tiktok.cap: What · How much · By when · Included · Not included. In that order.

instagram.cap: Save this and use it on your next quote, today.

facebook.body:
Five lines every quote needs, in this order:

1. What it is
2. How much
3. By when
4. What is included
5. What is not included

One screen, in the message itself, no attachment needed.

The fifth line is the one that wins work, and it is the one almost nobody writes.

Which of the five do you usually skip?

posts.why: Counterintuitive and immediately usable.

tiktok.hook: The "what's not included" line wins more jobs than the price does.
tiktok.vo: The what is not included line wins more jobs than the price does. It sounds honest, because it is, and because almost nobody writes it. It also prevents the argument in week three about whether the frame was part of it. One line, written before the problem exists, is worth more than a discount.
tiktok.cap: Write the awkward line early and you never have the awkward conversation.

instagram.cap: The exclusions line is the cheapest trust you can buy.

facebook.body:
The line that wins more jobs than the price is the one that says what is not included.

It sounds honest, because it is. Almost nobody writes it. And it prevents the argument in week three about whether the frame, the delivery, or the revision was part of the deal.

One line written before the problem exists is worth more than a discount.

Have you ever had that argument?

posts.topic: A date beat a cheaper price
posts.why: Directly attacks the assumption that price always wins.

tiktok.hook: A quote with a date beat a quote that was cheaper.
beats: So they paid more for certainty
tiktok.vo: A quote with a delivery date beat a quote that was fifteen thousand naira cheaper. The cheaper one had no date on it at all, so the customer could not plan their own week, and went with the one that told them exactly when it would be done. Certainty was worth fifteen thousand, and it cost the other vendor nothing to give it.
tiktok.cap: Certainty sold for ₦15,000 more, and it cost the winner nothing.

instagram.cap: The cheaper quote lost because it could not be planned around.

facebook.body:
A quote with a delivery date beat one that was ₦15,000 cheaper.

The cheaper quote had no date on it. The customer could not plan their own week around it, so they went with the one that told them exactly when the job would be done.

Certainty was worth ₦15,000. It cost the winning vendor nothing to give it.

What are you holding back that costs you nothing?

posts.why: A small, specific, instantly obeyed rule.

tiktok.hook: Never send a PDF as your first contact with a customer.
beats: Or they open it at work
Put the price in the message
tiktok.vo: Never send a PDF as your first contact. They will not open it, or they will open it in a queue and close it. Put the number in the message itself, one screen, no scrolling. Send the PDF after they have asked a second question, because then it is information instead of homework.
tiktok.cap: A PDF is homework. A message is a decision.

instagram.cap: Your quote is competing with forty notifications. Make it one screen.

facebook.body:
Never send a PDF as your first contact with a customer.

They will not open it. Or they will open it in a queue and close it before page two.

Put the number in the message itself. One screen. No scrolling.

Send the PDF after they have asked a second question — by then it is information rather than homework.

How do you send quotes?

posts.why: Names the exact sentence most people end quotes with.

tiktok.hook: "Let me know if you are interested" is homework for the customer.
tiktok.vo: Let me know if you are interested is homework. You have handed the customer a decision, no deadline, and no next step, and then you have left the room. Give them one question instead: shall I book the slot for Thursday. It has a date in it, so it can be answered.
tiktok.cap: End with a question that has a date inside it.

instagram.cap: Never end a message with an instruction to feel something.

facebook.body:
'Let me know if you're interested' is homework for the customer.

You have handed them a decision, no deadline and no next step, and then left the room.

End with one question that has a date inside it: 'Shall I book the slot for Thursday?'

That can be answered with one word. The other one cannot be answered at all.

What do you usually end with?

posts.topic: What makes you trust a quote?
posts.why: Witnesses validate the whole week's thesis.

tiktok.hook: I asked what makes people trust a quote. Nobody said the price.
tiktok.vo: I asked what makes people trust a quote. Nobody said the price. One said the detail, one said the date, and one said the line that told her what would not be done, because it was the only part that sounded like a person rather than a template. That is what you are competing on.
tiktok.cap: "They told me what they would not do." Not one person said price.

instagram.cap: Trust is built in the lines around the number, not in the number.

facebook.body:
I asked people what makes them trust a quote. Not one person said the price.

One said the detail. One said the delivery date. One said the line that told her what would not be done, because it was the only part that sounded like a person rather than a template.

That is what you are actually competing on.

What made you trust the last quote you accepted?

posts.topic: A job we could not deliver
posts.why: Losing work honestly is the most persuasive proof of standards.

tiktok.hook: We quoted six weeks on a job everyone else said three.
tiktok.vo: Someone asked us to quote a job for three weeks. We could not do it in three weeks without rushing something that would show. So we quoted six. They went with someone who said three, and I hope that person could actually do it. We lost the job and kept the standard, and I would do it again, which is easy to say and was not easy at the time.
tiktok.cap: We quoted the truth, lost the job, and would do it again.

instagram.cap: The fastest quote is not the same as the honest one.

facebook.body:
Someone asked us to quote a job for three weeks.

We could not do it in three weeks without rushing something that would show. So we quoted six.

They went with the person who said three. We lost the job and kept the standard.

I would do it again, which is easy to say now and was not easy at the time.

Have you ever lost work by being accurate?

posts.why: One small habit with an outsized effect on replies.

tiktok.hook: End every quote with one question: "Shall I book the slot?"
tiktok.vo: End every quote with one question: shall I book the slot. It is yes shaped, it takes one word to answer, and it implies there is a slot with value. Then stop typing. No second paragraph, no let me know, no thank you so much for your time. One question, and then silence, which is where the answer comes from.
tiktok.cap: One question. Then stop typing.

instagram.cap: "Shall I book the slot?" is the most answerable sentence in a quote.

facebook.body:
End every quote with one question: 'Shall I book the slot?'

It is yes-shaped. It takes one word to answer. It implies the slot has value and a date.

Then stop typing. No second paragraph. No 'let me know'. No thank you for your time.

One question, then silence — which is where the answer actually comes from.

Try it on your next quote and tell me what happens.
